contract_plain_english: The source asserts conservation of each spatially integrated conserved density through left endpoint flux minus right endpoint flux, and says the integral law remains fundamental for discontinuous solutions where the classical PDE fails (printed pp. 4–5, equation (1.10) and section 1.1.2). Finite volume methods approximate spatial cell averages, defined by dividing cell integrals by cell volumes, and update these values using edge fluxes estimated from approximate cell averages (printed p. 5, section 1.2). For neighboring cells, take Q_{i−1} as the left constant Riemann state and Q_i as the right constant state; solving the hyperbolic initial-value problem supplies information usable to compute a numerical flux and update cell averages over a time step (printed p. 5, equation (1.11) and following paragraph). The source leaves the jump-point value and numerical formulas unspecified, and qualifies its similarity-solution description as typical. These pages do not explicitly state a space-time rectangle theorem.
